shows: The Discover feed lists published notices, each with the buying authority, the contract value, the sector, when it was published and which source it came from. Every notice carries a relevance percentage in the top right: 92% for a National Supervised Toothbrushing Programme with Suffolk County Council at £227k, 78% for a Healthcare Offensive Waste collection with Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust at £1.5m, and 64% for M6 Lune Gorge Bored Piling Works with Kier Transportation Limited at £400k. The strapline reads "Live notices from Find a Tender and Contracts Finder, scored against what you can evidence today", and a filter row offers All sources, Find a Tender, Contracts Finder, Sector, Value and Relevance, with a counter reading "34 notices · updated 12 minutes ago". Each notice has Open in CrowMark, a link out to the source register, and Save.

The Tender questions screen breaks a live tender into its scored questions, headed by the contract name, £4,250,000 estimated value, PPN 002 and a deadline of 7 Jun 2026 for Northgate Borough Council, with a stage tab strip running Overview, Documents, Response, Review, Delivery and Outcome. A banner across the top states the grounding boundary in full: "Answers are AI-assisted and grounded only in your own answer library, the published requirement and your confirmed commitments. Every £ and % comes from your engine-computed commitments and is never invented. A named human reviews, edits and approves every answer before you submit it." Four questions are listed with their category, word limit and weighting, including Q4 Quality at a 750-word limit and weight 15 on mobilisation within eight weeks, Q7 Social value at 500 words and weight 10, and Q9 Compliance at 600 words and weight 10. Each row carries a Draft answer action, and the last one shows Review draft instead.

The Bid / no-bid screen gives a fit score of 87.2 out of 100 with a green Pursue recommendation, assessment confidence High, a contract value of £1,560,000 and 15 days to deadline, assessed against 17 recorded prior contracts. A Data confidence panel is marked "Not assessed" and explains that no comparable award history was found for this sector and CPV, then states in bold: "This is FIT context. It is not a probability of award, and CrowMark does not produce one." Below, "How the fit breaks down" itemises the score component by component with a band and a points total for each: Sector track record Strong at 22 of 22 points, Social-value readiness Strong at 20 of 20, Contract-size fit Strong at 18 of 18, and Mobilisation capacity Adequate at 14 of 20. Each component carries a one-line reason, such as "5 confirmed social-value measures ready to deploy. Social value carries 20% of the award."

The Evidence tracker follows a won contract into delivery, with a headline bar reading "This month's evidence coverage, 3 of 5 committed measures evidenced" at 60%, a 48-month duration and the next report due 1 Aug 2026. Three measure cards sit below, each with its own progress: Local employment at 1 of 4 (25%), Apprenticeships at 1 of 7 (14%) and Supported employment at 1 of 3 (33%). Each card lists the evidence item filed against it with a date and a view file link, such as "Signed employment contracts and payroll records for new local hires, 23 Jul 2026", and offers an Upload evidence button. A statutory strip runs along the bottom: s.52 requires contracts above £5m to carry at least three published KPIs, s.71 assessment is due in 4 months and is published every 12 months, and PPN 002 sets a 10% minimum weighting for social value.

The Answer library holds previously submitted answers and explains that "The drafter grounds new answers in these, and answers you marked as coming from a won bid rank higher as sources." A search field, a Newest first sort and an "Only answers from won bids" filter sit above a count of 10 answers. Three full answer texts are shown, on social value against the TOMs framework, on an eight-week mobilisation plan with TUPE consultation, and on safeguarding training to level 3 with DBS re-checks every three years. Each answer carries topic tags such as social-value, ppn-002, toms, mobilisation, tupe, safeguarding and compliance, and the first two are marked "From a won bid".

The Insights dashboard opens with four KPI tiles: 18 total contracts across 5 sectors, £1,284,000 social value delivered on won bids, 82% evidence completion of committed measures, and 2 s.71 assessments due within 90 days. A Contracts by status bar chart counts 3 Draft, 2 Profiling, 5 Evidence, 6 Won and 2 Lost, beside a Pipeline summary listing Active bids 4 at £6,410,000, Pending outcome 3 at £2,980,000, Won this period 6 at £9,240,000 and Draft 3 at £1,150,000. A Quick stats panel repeats pipeline value, won value, an average social-value score of 23.4% and 4 active bids, while Sector benchmarks for healthcare and social care show 5.2 average committed measures, average social value at 21.8% of contract value, the PPN 002 minimum weighting of 10% and local employment as the most common measure. A footnote reads: "Every figure is drawn from your own contract records and from published awards. CrowMark reports what has been evidenced and does not forecast outcomes."

The mobile Action centre opens with a "Due this week" card marked 4 open, noting that two evidence uploads and one s.71 assessment fall due before 1 August. Four task cards follow, each with a type chip, a countdown and the contract it belongs to: Evidence, due in 2 days, upload apprenticeship agreements for Reablement & Home Support; Duty, due in 6 days, publish s.71 assessment for the Highways Maintenance Term Contract; Review, due in 9 days, approve drafted answer Q7 for Grounds Maintenance, 3 lots; and Setup, due in 12 days, confirm social-value baseline for Managed Print, national. The buyer-side Social value requirement screen is in Draft for a £4,250,000 contract closing 7 Jun 2026 at Northgate Borough Council, with a BUYER badge on the product rail and a buyer navigation of Requirements, Responses, Evaluation, Suppliers, Delivery and Reports. Four figures head the page: a 20% social value weighting, noted as "Above the PPN 002 minimum of 10%", 5 criteria published each with its own evidence requirement, a total weight of 100% split Quality 50, Price 30, Social value 20, and 24 responses received from 24 invited suppliers. The Award criteria table lists five criteria, each with a TOMs reference, a weighting and the evidence that must be supplied: Local employment (TOMs NT1, weight 6%, signed contracts and payroll records), Apprenticeships and skills (NT3, 5%), SME and VCSE spend (NT9, 4%, a purchase ledger extract), Carbon reduction (NT12, 3%, a published dated plan) and Supported employment (NT5, 2%). Preview supplier view and Publish requirement actions sit at the top right.

The Response review screen takes one criterion, Local employment, criterion 1 of 5 at 6% weighting, for Meridian Care Group, response 4 of 24, with evaluator N. Blake named in the header. A banner states the boundary in full: "CrowMark locates the passage in the response that answers this criterion and shows you where it came from. It does not score, rank or recommend. The band below is yours to set, and every band on this evaluation was set by a named evaluator." The Located passage panel quotes the supplier verbatim, "We will create 14 new roles in the contracting authority's area within the first 12 months, recruited through the local JobCentre Plus and a partnership with Northgate College. Each role is a permanent contract at or above the real Living Wage", cites it to response document section 4.2, page 11, and traces it under "Where this came from" to the response document, the requirement criterion and the supplier commitment of 14 roles over 12 months. On the right, "Your band" offers four options with the note "Four bands. No half marks and no rounding", with Strong selected, and an audit line reading "Set by N. Blake · 24 Jul 2026 · recorded in the audit trail".

The Evaluation grid bands five suppliers against five criteria, with 24 responses, 5 criteria and 117 of 120 bands set, and a legend reading "Four bands, no half marks and no rounding: Strong, Adequate, Weak, Not answered". Every cell is a band rather than a number, so Meridian Care Group reads Strong, Strong, Adequate, Strong, Adequate, while Calder Health & Care Ltd reads Weak, Weak, Not answered, Adequate, Weak. An "Awaiting moderation" panel below flags three cases where two evaluators disagreed by more than one band, each with the reason and the two competing bands, such as Calder Health & Care Ltd on SME / VCSE spend, "No purchase ledger extract was attached to the response", Not answered versus Weak. A closing statement reads: "Every band on this evaluation was set by a named evaluator and is timestamped in the audit trail. CrowMark located the passage behind each one; it did not set, rank or recommend any band."
